title: Fuzzy clock showing wrong day of the week, calendar widget highlighting wrong day as being 'today'.
line: The Fuzzy Clock tooltip shows the correct weekday in the evening instead of the next or previous day.
explanation: The Clock type from libclock exposed dateTime as a QDateTime in UTC (shifted so that JavaScript would show local wall time). Bindings that qmlcachegen compiles to C++, like the Fuzzy Clock tooltip's Qt.locale().toString(currentDateTime, "dddd"), pass that QDateTime straight to QLocale, which formats it in UTC, so the weekday was the UTC one whenever the local date differs from the UTC date; the other tooltip lines go through JavaScript and were right. The change returns the same moment converted to local time, so compiled and JavaScript bindings agree.

commits.message:
libclock: return local time from dateTime

The dateTime property returned a UTC QDateTime, so compiled QML bindings
like the Fuzzy Clock tooltip's weekday formatted it as UTC and showed the
wrong day in the evening. Return the same moment in local time instead.

BUG: 519458

patches.diff:
From 89eb7a9ae97e3948945ccbce45de0d3e8903809f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 05:42:03 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] libclock: return local time from dateTime

The dateTime property returned a UTC QDateTime, so compiled QML bindings
like the Fuzzy Clock tooltip's weekday formatted it as UTC and showed the
wrong day in the evening. Return the same moment in local time instead.

BUG: 519458
---
 libclock/clock.cpp | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/libclock/clock.cpp b/libclock/clock.cpp
index f8f27c4bba..5c66eaa85e 100644
--- a/libclock/clock.cpp
+++ b/libclock/clock.cpp
@@ -115,7 +115,7 @@ QDateTime Clock::jsDateTime() const
     auto tzTime = nowUtc.toTimeZone(m_timeZone);
 
     // Javascript doesn't have a concept of timezones, only a value from UTC in the system timezone
-    return nowUtc.addSecs(-systemTime.offsetFromUtc() + tzTime.offsetFromUtc());
+    return nowUtc.addSecs(-systemTime.offsetFromUtc() + tzTime.offsetFromUtc()).toLocalTime();
 }
 
 QDateTime Clock::now() const
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Session in America/Chicago, Friday Nov 20 10:42 PM: the panel Fuzzy Clock tooltip says Saturday
Same setup with the fix: the tooltip says Friday

review.text: Clean, exact one-line root-cause fix in libclock: Clock::jsDateTime() shifted the UTC epoch so JS Date would display the target timezone's wall clock, but left the QDateTime in Qt::UTC, causing qmlcachegen AOT-compiled QLocale::toString bindings (such as Fuzzy Clock and Analog Clock tooltip weekdays) to format the UTC date instead. Converting the returned QDateTime with toLocalTime() preserves the exact epoch milliseconds for JavaScript while aligning C++/AOT formatting with local wall time. Before/after screenshots clearly confirm the fix, and the non-reproducing calendar highlight symptom from 6.6.4 is honestly noted.

reviews.text: Clean, exact one-line root-cause fix in libclock: Clock::jsDateTime() shifted the UTC epoch so JS Date would display the target timezone's wall clock, but left the QDateTime in Qt::UTC, causing qmlcachegen AOT-compiled QLocale::toString bindings (such as Fuzzy Clock and Analog Clock tooltip weekdays) to format the UTC date instead. Converting the returned QDateTime with toLocalTime() preserves the exact epoch milliseconds for JavaScript while aligning C++/AOT formatting with local wall time. Before/after screenshots clearly confirm the fix, and the non-reproducing calendar highlight symptom from 6.6.4 is honestly noted.

Good root-cause work. Clock::jsDateTime returns a UTC-spec QDateTime shifted for JavaScript, so AOT-compiled bindings that hand it straight to QLocale (Fuzzy, Analog and Binary Clock 'dddd') format it in UTC and get the wrong weekday in the evening. toLocalTime() keeps the same instant, so the JavaScript Date paths (getHours, date arithmetic, the Digital Clock offsets) are unchanged while compiled bindings and C++ consumers such as the calendar's today now see local wall time; fixing it once in libclock is the right layer. The before/after tooltips (Saturday vs Friday at 10:4x PM Chicago) prove it, and the commit text matches the one-line diff.
